text:
jordan: heads-up — nightly eval for quant-ggml-3b (run id e2f9) shows a large uptick in prompt failure rate vs baseline, started at 03:12 UTC

maya: noted. failure pattern? rogue hallucinations or missing completions?

jordan: mostly bad completions and higher entropy. pass_rate dropped from 92% -> 68% on our 150-shot regression set. quick grep in logs shows sampling params different for some shards.

raul: any config drift? the harness should pin sampling.

jordan: here's snippet from the eval-run log for a failing job ->
```json
{"run_id":"e2f9","model":"quant-ggml-3b","sampling":{"temperature":1.2,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":0},"seed":null}
```

maya: seed=null is suspicious. we should always seed nightly deterministically. maybe a code path fell back to env override.

ci-bot: pipeline status: nightly-evals/quant-ggml-3b #283 failed checks (regression detected). See: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/283

liz: I remember a recent change in the quant fallback logic that injects `EVAL_SAMPLING_OVERRIDE` for models with certain kernels. could be leaking into harness.

sam: @liz can you point to the PR?

liz: PR #4823 — 'quant: runtime fallback sampling override for low-latency path' (merged two days ago). it sets sampling.temperature = env.TEMP_OVERRIDE when using the fast-quant engine.

raul: that explains temperature=1.2. but why seed=null? the harness normally sets SEED from timestamp. maybe the override path bypasses seeding.

jordan: minimal repro to confirm:
```bash
# repro locally
EVAL_SAMPLING_OVERRIDE=1.2 ./eval_harness --model quant-ggml-3b --seed $(date +%s) --prompt-set nightly_regressions
```

maya: running that now on my laptop. will report quick stats. :eyes:

maya: quick run shows same weird high-entropy outputs when override set and no explicit --seed passed. when I pass --seed 42 the outputs are consistent but still lower quality vs baseline temp=0.8.

sam: so two issues: (1) override changes temp causing quality hit; (2) seeding not propagated in fast path leading to nondeterminism. we should triage both.

raul: immediate mitigation: revert env-based override in prod-nightly, or add assertion in harness that sampling params match expected.

jordan: propose 1) pin nightly to config file (no env overrides) and 2) add harness assertion: fail eval if sampling != expected for that job. I'll submit a patch.

liz: also add a unit test that ensures seeding is set when eval_harness invoked, and that env.TEMP_OVERRIDE must be explicit in job config (not auto-injected).

sam: I'll run a targeted rerun of the failing nightly with pinned params and explicit seed to check recovery. target: rerun #283 with temp=0.8 seed=161803398.

ci-bot: triggered rerun: nightly-evals/quant-ggml-3b #283.rerun1 (pinned sampling).

maya: rerun coming back — preliminary pass_rate 91% for the pinned job. looks like override was the main regression vector.

raul: great. next steps:
- backfill PR to remove implicit override from runtime (liz)
- add harness assertion + unit test (jordan + liz)
- add canary for sampling-param drift alert in Console (sam)

jordan: I filed issues: https://issues.internal/RED-ml/814 (remove implicit override), https://issues.internal/RED-ml/815 (harness assertion).

liz: assigning to myself for the runtime PR, will target hotfix today.

sam: I'll draft the canary rule: alert when nightly sampling param differs from job config for >1 shard.

maya: leaving logs at /tmp/nightly/e2f9-logs.tar.gz and uploading to the #eng-ml shared S3: s3://redwood-debug/nightly/e2f9/e2f9-logs.tar.gz

jordan: thanks all. good catch. follow-ups in the two issues. :raised_hands:
